result.summary: Profile delete confirmation (confirmView) uses deleteHold; heldButton's allowed() gates the hold; mode 'delete' had no draft; tests open it via profile(name).remove.click() and act(), 32 hold tests press 'Endgültig löschen' directly.

confirmView adds a name field (label 'Zum Bestätigen den Namen „<name>“ eingeben', focused, spellcheck/correct off, draft kept in the delete mode); deleteHold takes an optional armed check: aria-disabled until NFC-trimmed text equals the stored name, a hold before that shows a German refusal and deletes nothing; act also re-checks. Own concepts and examples keep the plain hold. Test harness act() types the name for existing hold tests (typeDeleteName:false for new ones); 2 new tests; 6 updated for texts/focus. Docs caregiver.md; CSS label spacing. npm run verify passed: 659 node tests; browser 4 pass 2 skipped. Hand-run Chromium: button aria-disabled true for 'Testki', false for 'Testkind', no console errors.

observations: src/caregiver.ts:3058 rearm() only flips aria-disabled; after a refused press the hint keeps 'Der Name stimmt noch nicht...' even once the correct name is typed, until the next press. Consider resetting the hint to DELETE_HOLD_HINT when ok() becomes true.

src/caregiver.ts:3126 if the name is changed to a wrong one during a running hold, the release deletes nothing but act() returns false after idle(), so the line shows the plain hold hint instead of the German wrong-name refusal.

test/caregiver.test.mjs:7319 the unarmed refusal is tested only with a pointer hold; no test holds Enter/Space on 'Endgültig löschen' with an empty or wrong name (same allowed() path, inferred safe). Harness act()/confirmDelete auto-typing would mask a lost-draft regression in act-based tests; only the gated redraw test at :4457 covers draft survival implicitly.
result.summary: Correctness review of dcaceca: no path deletes without the typed name. Pointer and Enter/Space both go through heldButton.start -> allowed(), which refuses with the German line while named() is false (src/caregiver.ts:3074-3081); the act re-checks named() at release (3126), so editing the field during a running hold cannot delete; stale buttons stay blocked by current(). Draft text lives on the mode object (draft.typed) and is rebuilt into the new field on every redraw (3113-3116, 3130-3133); the gated-redraw hold test only deletes via the second button if the text survived. Focus goes to delete-name on open (3186); Escape leaves via leaveMode back to delete:<id> (test added). Field label and comparison use profile.displayName (stored, NFC/trimmed by makeProfile), the title keeps the (2) label. Own-concept/example deletes keep armed=null. Harness auto-typing is limited to an empty, not-yet-autotyped field and opt-out exists; the new tests use typeDeleteName:false.

observations: src/caregiver.ts:3118 names that look the same but are not typed the same are refused with no hint why: inner double spaces or a no-break space (kept by normalizeDisplayName, collapsed when HTML shows the label), or emoji with/without variation selector U+FE0F. Workaround is renaming first; consider comparing with inner whitespace collapsed or saying so in the refusal.

public/styles.css:247 .caregiver-delete-name-label has no overflow-wrap:anywhere (the confirm title and profile name have it); a 40-character name without spaces can overflow the label at phone width.

src/caregiver.ts:3186 focus now opens on the name field, so a screen reader starts at the field label and can skip the title and the loss text ('Alle ausgewählten Begriffe ... gehen verloren'); consider aria-describedby on the field pointing at the loss text. Not checked with assistive technology.
result.summary: Blind-spot review of dcaceca (accessibility, hard-to-type names, child safety). No blocking gap: the field is labelled with the stored name, aria-disabled plus a role=status refusal line tells assistive tech why the hold does nothing, Escape/Abbrechen still leave, and a profile whose name proves hard to type can still be renamed to a plain name and then deleted, so no profile becomes undeletable. Stored names are NFC and trimmed by normalizeDisplayName (src/profiles/profile.ts:66-77), so the NFC/trim comparison at src/caregiver.ts:3118 cannot fail on normalization alone. The child-safety claim is bounded honestly in docs/caregiver.md (a reader who can type the shown name can delete; not security). Non-blocking limits recorded as observations.
